cues.text: A family in Ealing
Bukayo Saka was born in 2001 in Ealing, in London.
His parents, Adenike and Yomi, had moved to London from Nigeria to find work.
Bukayo did very well at school, with top grades in his exams.
Lift the flap to see who kept him steady.
Bukayo has called his dad, Yomi, a massive inspiration.
He said that from when he was young, his dad always kept him grounded and humble.
Family can be your anchor. Stay close to the people who keep you steady.
Little Chilli
At seven, Bukayo joined Arsenal’s youth academy at Hale End.
He was not the biggest player.
His captain later nicknamed him Little Chilli, because he had so much energy and power, and was quite small.
His youth coach said Bukayo always stood out, with a really good character.
Flip the shirt.
In 2018, at seventeen, Bukayo played his first game for the first team.
He played wherever the team needed him, on the wing, and even at left-back.
Being small doesn’t make you less. Your energy and your heart count too.
The fifth penalty
In 2021, England reached the final of Euro 2020 against Italy, at Wembley in London.
Bukayo was nineteen.
He came on as a substitute, and after extra time the final went to a penalty shoot-out.
Bukayo was chosen to take England’s fifth penalty.
It was his first penalty for England’s senior team.
Many people would feel nervous.
Kick the ball.
The goalkeeper, Gianluigi Donnarumma, saved it, and Italy won the cup.
Being brave doesn’t always mean winning. Trying when it’s hard takes courage.
Unkind words
After the final, Bukayo and two teammates who had also missed, Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho, were sent hurtful racist messages online.
Some people attacked them because of the colour of their skin.
That is never okay.
Raise the shield.
Bukayo spoke up.
He said he knew straight away the kind of hate he would receive, and that social media companies were not doing enough to stop these messages.
If someone is unkind to you online, you are not alone. Tell a grown-up you trust.
Hearts and messages
Many people stood with Bukayo.
The Football Association said the abuse was wrong, and promised to do all it could to support the players.
The Prime Minister and Prince William spoke out against the racism too.
Lift the three hearts.
In Manchester, a digital mural showing Bukayo, Marcus and Jadon was unveiled.
Within three days, all three players thanked people for the support they had received.
Kind words can be louder than cruel ones. Be the one who sends kindness.
Stepping up again
Bukayo kept going.
In 2022, and again in 2023, he was named England Men’s Player of the Year.
At Euro 2024, England played Switzerland in the quarter-final, and Bukayo scored to make it 1–1.
The game went to a penalty shoot-out again.
Kick the ball.
Just like three years before, Bukayo stepped up.
This time he scored, England went through, and he was named player of the match.
One hard moment does not decide your future. You can step up again.
